title: Learn Grafana for Go Services
description: Build a working observability stack, write PromQL, create dashboards and alerts, instrument Go, and provision Grafana from files.

lessons.title: What Is Grafana?
lessons.instruction: Grafana queries and visualizes observability data; Prometheus, not Grafana, scrapes and stores these metrics. Open Grafana from the lab panel, sign in with admin / admin, and verify its API and database are healthy.

lessons.title: The Observability Stack
lessons.instruction: The Go service exposes metrics, Prometheus scrapes and stores them, and Grafana queries Prometheus. Open all three lab links and confirm every service and the go-lab scrape target are healthy.

lessons.title: Install Grafana
lessons.instruction: The lab already runs Grafana 13.2.0 in Docker, so this exercise inspects that installation rather than installing another copy. Open Administration → General → Stats and confirm the version and database.

lessons.title: The Grafana UI
lessons.instruction: Dashboards contain panels that turn queries into visualizations. Choose Dashboards → New → New dashboard, add any visualization titled Read Run UI Tour, and save the dashboard.

lessons.title: Organizations
lessons.instruction: Organizations isolate data sources, dashboards, and users; folders organize dashboards within one organization. Open Administration → General → Organizations and create Read Run Lab, but continue the course in the default organization.

lessons.title: Data Sources
lessons.instruction: A data source tells Grafana where and how to query external data. Open Connections → Data sources → Add new data source, choose Prometheus, name it Read Run Prometheus, and save it.

lessons.title: Add Prometheus
lessons.instruction: Grafana runs in a container, so it reaches Prometheus by service name rather than localhost. Edit Read Run Prometheus, set the server URL to http://prometheus:9090, keep Server access, enable Default, and save.

lessons.title: Test the Connection
lessons.instruction: Save & test proves Grafana can reach the Prometheus API, but not that every scrape target is healthy. Open Read Run Prometheus, click Save & test, and confirm the API query succeeds.

lessons.title: Scrape Targets
lessons.instruction: A target is UP when its latest Prometheus scrape succeeded. Open Prometheus, choose Status → Target health, and confirm the go-lab job endpoint is UP.

lessons.title: Explore
lessons.instruction: Explore is Grafana's workspace for testing queries before turning them into panels. Select Read Run Prometheus, run go_lab_requests_total, add the result to Read Run UI Tour, and save the dashboard.

lessons.title: Metric Selectors
lessons.instruction: A metric-name selector returns an instant vector containing every live series with that name. Enter go_lab_requests_total and confirm it returns data.

lessons.title: Labels
lessons.instruction: Labels identify dimensions of a metric and matchers select specific series. Filter go_lab_requests_total with the exact matcher job="go-lab".

lessons.title: Range Vectors
lessons.instruction: A range selector supplies each series' samples from a lookback window; it is separate from Grafana's dashboard time range. Select five minutes with go_lab_requests_total[5m].

lessons.title: Rate
lessons.instruction: rate handles counter resets and estimates the average per-second increase across a range. Convert the request counter with rate(go_lab_requests_total[5m]).

lessons.title: Aggregations
lessons.instruction: An aggregation combines series and discards labels unless they are retained by its grouping clause. Return request rate per job with sum by (job) (rate(go_lab_requests_total[5m])).

lessons.title: First Dashboard
lessons.instruction: A dashboard is a saved container for related panels and controls. Choose Dashboards → New → New dashboard and save it as Read Run Go Service.

lessons.title: Panels
lessons.instruction: A panel binds a data-source query to a visualization. Edit Read Run Go Service and add a time-series panel using Read Run Prometheus and rate(go_lab_requests_total[5m]); give it a useful title, apply, and save.

lessons.title: Time Ranges
lessons.instruction: The dashboard time range controls the interval sent to its panels, and saving it sets the dashboard default. Open Read Run Go Service, choose Last 6 hours, then save and include the current range.

lessons.title: Dashboard Variables
lessons.instruction: Variables make one dashboard reusable by supplying values to panel queries. In Read Run Go Service, add a Query variable named job using Read Run Prometheus and label_values(go_lab_requests_total, job), then save.

lessons.title: Dashboard JSON
lessons.instruction: A dashboard's JSON model carries its portable structure, including panels and templating. Open Read Run Go Service → Dashboard settings → JSON model and copy it into the editor, retaining the title, panels, and job variable.

lessons.title: Alert Rules
lessons.instruction: An alert rule evaluates a query on a schedule and compares the result with a condition. Create High Request Rate under Alerting → Alert rules using Read Run Prometheus, rate(go_lab_requests_total[5m]), a threshold, a folder, and an evaluation group; then save.

lessons.title: Expressions
lessons.instruction: A Reduce expression turns each returned series into one value that a threshold can evaluate. Edit High Request Rate, add Reduce between the Prometheus query and threshold, and save.

lessons.title: Contact Points
lessons.instruction: A contact point defines where notifications are delivered; routing is configured separately. Open Alerting → Contact points and save a Webhook named Read Run Contact with URL http://metrics:8081/alerts.

lessons.title: Notification Policies
lessons.instruction: Notification policies form a routing tree that sends matching alerts to contact points. Open Alerting → Notification policies and route the default policy or a matching child policy to Read Run Contact, then save.

lessons.title: Silences
lessons.instruction: A silence suppresses matching notifications for a fixed period; the alert rule still evaluates. Open Alerting → Silences → Add silence, match High Request Rate, include that name in the comment, choose a short duration, and submit.

lessons.title: Prometheus Text Format
lessons.instruction: Prometheus exposition is line-oriented: metadata declares the metric type and a sample supplies its value. Complete both Println calls to emit exactly # TYPE requests_total counter followed by requests_total 7.

lessons.title: Metrics Handler
lessons.instruction: A metrics handler exposes samples over HTTP for Prometheus to scrape. This exercise writes the text format directly; production services usually use a client library. Implement metrics to write requests_total 3 to the ResponseWriter.

lessons.title: Counters
lessons.instruction: A counter only increases during a process lifetime and resets when the process restarts. Increment requests once for each handled request, then print the final value 3.

lessons.title: Gauges
lessons.instruction: A gauge can rise and fall, making it suitable for current values such as in-flight work. Start active at 2; print it, increment and print when a request begins, then decrement and print when it completes.
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	active := 2
	fmt.Println(active)
	active++
	fmt.Println(active)
	active--
	fmt.Println(active)
}

lessons.title: Histograms
lessons.instruction: Histogram buckets are cumulative: an le="0.5" bucket counts every observation at or below 0.5 seconds. Count those observations and print request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.5"} 2.

lessons.title: Provisioning
lessons.instruction: Provisioning makes Grafana resources reproducible from files, and later file reloads can replace UI changes. In the apiVersion 1 dashboard provider for Read Run Provider, set options.path to /var/lib/grafana/dashboards so Grafana loads Provider Check.
lessons.starter:
apiVersion: 1

providers:
  - name: Read Run Provider
    orgId: 1
    folder: Read Run Provisioned
    type: file
    disableDeletion: false
    updateIntervalSeconds: 10
    options:
      path: TODO

lessons.title: Folders and Permissions
lessons.instruction: Folders organize dashboards and provide a boundary for inherited access within an organization. Create Read Run Operations, open its permissions, add at least one explicit user, team, or role permission, and save.

lessons.title: Data Source Provisioning
lessons.instruction: A stable UID lets dashboards reference a provisioned data source, while editable false keeps the file authoritative. Set Provisioned Prometheus, UID provisioned-prometheus, to http://prometheus:9090 and keep editable false.
lessons.starter:
apiVersion: 1

datasources:
  - name: Provisioned Prometheus
    uid: provisioned-prometheus
    type: prometheus
    access: proxy
    url: TODO
    isDefault: false
    editable: false

lessons.title: Dashboard Provisioning
lessons.instruction: Grafana's file provider loads valid dashboard JSON, and the UID supplies stable identity across reloads. Set UID read-run-provisioned and title Read Run Provisioned; keep schemaVersion 39 and panels valid.

lessons.title: Backups
lessons.instruction: A dashboard export can restore that dashboard, but it is not a full backup of Grafana's database, configuration, or secrets. Export Read Run Go Service and paste its complete JSON model here, retaining UID read-run-go, title, and panels.
